properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured on main): to change an existing node, reflow2's route is to call its add_* constructor again with the same id. 21 tools' descriptions say so, but none in its first sentence, which is the whole summary find_tools returns. And no served tool is named for updating. So "update properties of an existing node" ranks add_artifact outside the first 40 on 0.76.0, 0.78.0 and main, and a guessed update_node is refused
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-05, triaging the entry appended to art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05 the same day (lines 326-334). Binaries: 0.76.0 and 0.78.0 release builds, and main at e7e304d (reports 0.78.0); scratch stores under the hub session's scratchpad, isolated HOME.

① OBSERVED, the reporter's words (0.76.0): marking an Artifact `realized`, "`find_tools` for 'update properties of an existing node' returned `set_capability_status` / `set_requirement_status` / `create_node`, no artifact status setter; guessed `--call update_node` → `no tool named `update_node` is served`. Re-calling `add_artifact` with the same `id` upserted (receipt showed new status). Likewise re-calling `realizes` updated the edge's `conformance` in place … Inferred: the upsert behaviour works but is undiscoverable." NOT AFFECTED: the upsert itself works.

② PRECEDENT: searched (update_node, "no tool named", re-call, update an existing). No finding records discoverability of the revise route. chg:bl183-constructors-merge built the merge-on-revise behaviour.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) an artifact status setter exists and find_tools ranks it low; (b) the revise route exists but find_tools' summary never says so; (c) find_tools does not search far enough into descriptions; (d) the observation is wrong.

⑤ MEASURED, the same on 0.76.0, 0.78.0 and main:
- No artifact status setter is served. The Artifact tools are add_artifact, link_artifact, reconcile_artifacts, set_artifact_checksum(s) and set_artifact_intent (granularity and stance, not status). add_artifact's `status` parameter and `link_artifact` are the only status routes. (a) is refuted.
- `find_tools {query: "update properties of an existing node", limit: 40}`: top 5 on 0.76.0 create_nodes, scan_nodes, set_provenance, create_node, add_actor, and on 0.78.0 and main create_nodes, get_node, set_provenance, scan_nodes, create_node; add_artifact is not in the 40. (The reporter's top hits differed, set_capability_status and set_requirement_status among them; their design and limit are unknown.) "update an existing node" ranks add_artifact 24th. "mark an artifact realized" ranks it 1st. So find_tools finds add_artifact by the noun, never by the verb.
- add_artifact's summary in find_tools is "Create an Artifact node — a real deliverable (file/spec/doc) that lives outside the graph, pointed to by `location`." find_tools' summary is trim_summary(description) (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/service.rs:1129), the first sentence. Of the 21 tools whose description says a re-call with the same id revises ("CONTENT FIELDS ARE REQUIRED TO CREATE AND OPTIONAL TO REVISE" or "REVISES"), none says it in the first sentence. (b) holds.
- `--call update_node` is refused on all three: "no tool named `update_node` is served … `--call find_tools` finds one".
- Since 0.78.0, `--describe add_artifact` prints the revise sentence, and its `id` parameter says "Calling again with an EXISTING id REVISES that node". That needs the agent to have picked add_artifact first, which the update query does not lead to.
(c) is refuted for this case: BM25 reads the whole description, but the descriptions say "revises", not "update" or "edit".

⑥ CLASS: a tool's second role is written in its body and never in the line a catalogue shows, and the role's verb (update) appears nowhere. It is the same placement class as fact:defect-the-commonest-changeevent-mistake-was-fixed-in-the-description-and-a-third-project-hit-it-anyway: the text exists where it is not read.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the fix is the first sentence of each dual-mode constructor, an update/revise alias in find_tools' vocabulary, or a refusal for update_node that names the add_* route. Not chosen here.
